coreValues.title:
Four systems that turn
your mistakes into assets
coreValues.kicker: Writing, analysis, accumulation, and growth all run in one place. A personal mistake notebook for learners, a class-management toolkit for professors.

items.title: AI mistake notebook
items.body: Your error records build up automatically → personal DB → a virtuous cycle of better feedback. The more you use it, the smarter it gets.

items.title: Flipped learning
items.body: Write first drafts at home; do AI practice, theory, and revisions in class. Focus professors' time on what matters most.

items.title: Gamification
items.body: Badges, levels, streaks, and sound effects keep learners motivated. Even day-one students start having fun.

items.title: Custom chatbot
items.body: Uses the professor's corpus as a RAG knowledge base. Becomes a different AI tutor for each class.

demo.title: Here's how it flows — AI analyzes in real time
demo.kicker: Write on the left, error cards top-right, AI tutor chat bottom-right. As the learner types, analysis, highlights, cards, and solutions appear in sequence.
demo.analyzingTip: Claude API is analyzing your sentences…
demo.cardEmpty: Start writing and your error cards will appear here
demo.explainText: A time-duration complement must come after the verb.
demo.chatAiQuestion: Would you like me to explain in more detail why this is a word-order error? I can also show you similar time-duration-complement examples.
demo.chatPlaceholder: Ask me anything — grammar, vocabulary, whatever…

flow.title:
A growth cycle that runs
in five steps
flow.kicker: Not write-once-and-done, but a virtuous cycle where data accumulates and feedback gets sharper every time you write.

steps.title: Write
steps.body: The learner enters Chinese text they wrote themselves — assignment submissions or free writing, either works.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.body: Claude API identifies vocabulary and grammar errors and builds its rationale through CoT step-by-step reasoning.

steps.title: Error cards
steps.body: Cards generated with 4 fields (range / type / fix / explanation) plus HSK tags and fossilization warnings.

steps.title: Accumulate
steps.body: Error cards build up in a personal DB, automatically detecting fossilization and weak areas.

steps.title: Report
steps.body: A weekly card-news digest is emailed out, and your semester growth graph updates.

gamification.title:
So leveling up
means skilling up
gamification.kicker: Badges, levels, streaks, and sound effects keep learners motivated. Even first-years just starting out can jump in with ease.
gamification.soundNote: Sound effect plays on unlock — correct.mp3 / streak.mp3 / level-up.mp3

professor.title:
Secure feedback quality
without any student data.
professor.kicker: Once a professor uploads a corpus, it works as a per-class RAG knowledge base from that day on. Real-time mode and the marketplace help you run your classes.

cards.title: Corpus upload
cards.body: Practical Modern Chinese Grammar PDFs, lecture-material DOCX, HSK writing-corpus TXT — auto-inserted into that class's Claude prompt the moment you upload.

cards.title: Real-time in-class mode
cards.body: Hit Start class → live aggregation of every student's error types every 5 seconds. The TOP 3 errors are shown instantly for use in board work and follow-up explanations.

cards.title: Resource marketplace
cards.body: Search, download, and instantly apply other professors' public corpora and ICL examples. Creates a network effect across Chinese departments nationwide.

partners.title:
Built together with
Chinese departments nationwide
partners.kicker: We incorporate feedback from professors and learners in the field every week. The goal isn't one school's tool, but infrastructure for Chinese-language education across Korea.
partners.ctaStrong: We're looking for schools to join us.
partners.ctaRest: We provide pre-semester workshops, professor corpus setup, and free pilot programs.
partners.videoUniversities: Kyonggi University × Sogang University × Seoul National University × Duksung Women's University

cta.sub: Free for students. Professors can upload a corpus and run a class the moment they open it. With PWA, it works the same on mobile.
